summary: Interpreted the receipt carrying the rejection operands (CheckRun dd6a5001bf7f487994e7ec6dd674bb02: completed, tests_passed, exit 0, 21 parsed observations, 0 parse errors) and the operands split the verdict rather than settling it. Indices 17-19 show the same entry rejected three times - index 4, term 2, one change, joint-entering - by three different nodes (3, 1, 4) at seed 35, steps 22/23/31, with reason 'config is already joint'; index 20 reports three rejections among 245 configuration changes with violations=0. Two constraints: the entry is identical each time, so the phenomenon is about one log position rather than three independent proposals; and every rejecting node reports applied=4 and committed=4, so it was not application-lagging - which refutes the lag-based reading the earlier interpretations leaned on and also refutes my own earlier framing that the shape arises only when a node's application is behind. The blocker is that applied equals the index of the entry being applied (4), precisely what a double application or an off-by-one in the harness's apply bookkeeping would look like, and the harness does rebuild nodes at restart events with Config.Applied taken from the node's applied index, so that possibility cannot be excluded from these four indices. The account is therefore narrowed to two live readings - a target-side log-order shape in which a joint-entering change reaches a node whose tracker is joint with no lag involved (availability-relevant), or a harness artifact where an already-applied entry is re-presented (in which case the earlier refutation of the panic path stands) - and the discriminator is named: print the node's applied and applying pointers plus the batch's first and last entry indexes before each apply, and flag any batch starting at or below applied; a re-applied batch confirms the artifact and voids the rejection count, while a batch starting at applied+1 for the rejecting node means the log genuinely carried that change there. Counterevidence and limits recorded as well: violations=0 alongside the rejections, all three occurrences from one seed and one entry, the restart path is exactly the uninstrumented code that could re-present entries, the receipt lacks applying/batch/surrounding-entry data, no rejection was observed at a leader, and only the first three occurrences emit operands though the counter counts all.
